reasons.plausibility: Al additions to BCC refractory high-entropy alloys typically promote brittle intermetallic phases (e.g., B2, Laves) rather than maintaining a single-phase BCC solid solution, making the predicted retention of strength and ductility unlikely.
reasons.testability: The proposed experiment is clearly defined with specific compositions, processing, test conditions, and quantitative rejection criteria based on density and yield strength.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses the core trade-off but proposes a well-known embrittling element (Al) without acknowledging the extensive literature showing it degrades ductility in similar RHEAs, limiting its practical value.
